classification: Frozen fictional profiles with a separate profile-inferred comparison round. First offers preserve original answers; current offers include comparison answers and a new frozen plain-language defining-work round. Earlier 0.42 checks remain available in the history. These are simulations, not recorded student behavior.

methods: The original 76-offer review remains a historical cohort. The 0.44 rerun uses newly versioned defining-work questions and separately frozen profile-only answers; the chart shows each reviewed offer’s current status.
Preserve every original profile and work answer. Freeze the initially offered up to three profession comparisons per model before new answer authoring.

Additional answers are inferred by separate authors given only biographies and question/option text, with evidence and uncertainty; answers are frozen before final matching. Existing answers are reused, not replaced.

Run planMatchCandidates across explored fields and focused checks. Top requires two separate defining-work interests plus existing profile, task and clinical gates. Medium or high confidence inferred Yes answers can support interest; low confidence, uncertainty, unfamiliarity or No cannot. Existing tools, specialist variants and prior professional experience are not interest prerequisites. Independent supporting question groups measure evidence breadth; short checks do not gain a percentage advantage.

Education preferences and realistic first-paid-stage pay order comparably supported matches. Comparisons awaiting review are invitations. Pending core interests appear under Needs confirmation. Starting-pay coverage remains a separate financial assessment.
Lifestyle options use the same five education groups and five-per-group cap, deduplicated across groups.
A lifestyle option must cover its monthly budget at the first paid stage, meet the displayed gross-income threshold, and not require prior role experience.
Stored career previews are comparisons, not recorded career choices.
